title: Legacy C++ Sensor Integration
business: Industrial IoT manufacturers maintaining legacy C++ firmware for sensor data processing.
problem: Frequent memory corruption and data races occur when manual memory management is used to bridge high-speed sensor data into modern application logic.
solution: Swift provides native interoperability with C++ types, allowing developers to wrap legacy sensor processing routines in a memory-safe environment without requiring a full rewrite of the existing C++ codebase.
steps: Identify the existing C++ sensor data structures and processing functions.
Import the C++ headers into the Swift project using the native C++ interoperability layer.
Define Swift-side wrappers that utilize Swift's strong type system to encapsulate C++ pointers.
Implement data processing logic in Swift, leveraging compile-time memory safety guarantees.
Verify that the Swift-wrapped code interacts correctly with the underlying C++ memory buffers.
outcome: A more robust sensor processing pipeline where memory safety is enforced at compile time, reducing runtime crashes caused by invalid pointer access.
limitation: Swift's interoperability relies on the compiler's ability to map C++ types; complex template-heavy C++ code may require manual bridging or simplification, which can be verified by checking the compiler's ability to generate the corresponding Swift interface.
